Throw grand masquerades and cruise back alleys while evading moralistic constables who seek to destroy your community. Be careful, there may even be informers in your midst! Players draft hands of vice cards representing the different gestures, desires, and encounters that were frowned upon by the Society for the Reformation of Manners, a citizen group that sought to stamp out any behavior it deemed deviant in late 17th and early 18th century London. These cards allow players to host festivities with the help of their fellow mollies and create joy. But, those same cards can also lead players to be arrested and to the ultimate ruin of the molly house. As players encounter the Society’s enforcers, they will often have to pay bribes or may be coerced into becoming informers for the Society. Informers must try desperately to undermine the community around Mother Clap’s Molly House without being discovered by their fellow mollies. Christening: Queen and 3 desire cards of the same value. Dance: Jack and 3 desire cards in sequential order (ignore suit). If none of the above ranks are made, a Quiet Gathering occurs. The four lowest desires are selected as the winning set, ignoring rogues. If there were fewer than four desires played, score only those. [Rating: 1/10] The game is built around a semi-cooperative card playing system, maybe there's some promise there, but everything built from it is confusing. You're sorta rolling to move around the board, but the dice system is so generous that you can usually decide where to go anyway. You're picking up public cards so it's not a tense card match, they're just pieces to complete a minigame and score VP. So I guess it's more of a hidden traitor game, but that's such an afterthought that it's not even the central tension, just a way to possibly counter someone scoring high? [Rating: 1/10] Read through the rulebook like 3 times. We still have no idea how to play this. Theme and gameplay are in huge disconnected. Half the rules make no sense.

[Rating: 1/10] It's a shame that other games from this company are really well done, but this game has no appeal as the theme is just pasted on to a very mediocre system. I am not interested in playing this at all.

[Rating: 1/10] Interesting theme and presentation but terribly inelegant, unintuitive rule set. Combine that with lots of randomness and limited decision space and you end up with a very unsatisfying experience. Hard pass.

[Rating: 1/10] As usual it's an ambitious design but this semi-coop-card play game just doesn't hang together. Too much chaos (hand draw, market draw, roll to move, cards going into the gossip deck, party tricks) for my taste and decisions rarely feel like they have an impact. Note we ran it twice back to back and I'd recommend that as Molly House has enough opacity that your first play may fall flat. Overall a big miss, pour moi. Visually and thematically it's a stellar production, loved the card art with historical references and the board is gorgeous. But would never play again.

[Rating: 1/10] A very weird game that combines classic roll and move around a board like in Monopoly/Talisman and playing card combinations "cooperatively" like in Surfosaurus Rex/Combo with a lot more rules and details.  For how long and convoluted it is, there's a lot of luck involved. I think the game tries to mitigate this through bluffing and negotiation (two things I don't like), but it's not enough. Heck, you can can even lose to a die roll right at the end even if you were ahead of everyone else.  I love the theme, if that counts for anything.  I wouldn't play it ever again.

[Rating: 1/10] I wrote an honest review, but it looks like some people do not want this game to be rated according to quality, but rather push it high for marketing reasons. What a shame, also furious that BGG allows censorship for Capital reasons.  Anyhow, we played it once, it's a mix of the gang and monopoly, doesn't really work at all, the person who bought it sold it quickly, This game kind of defies game description and honestly I don't think that it can be fixed, the core of the game is not there.

[Rating: 1/10] I like the theme. And that's probably the only thing I like about this game. The actual game is random, nearly unplayable mess.

[Rating: 2/10] So far a huge let down from John Company second edition. When I saw a new wehrle game my credit card lept out of my pocket. But digging deeper just not the same. Similar disappointment  with newest pax release funnily enough. Favorite game, favorite series respectively, each new release what feels more Hollandspiele. Maybe this is otherwise an experiment and for fun between greatness, don’t know. Hope so. Feels more “for fun” and theme forward than the pure gaming greatness of JC. [Rating: 2/10] Trips over its own shoes all too often in too many ways. Rulebook clunky, choppy flow, etc. Surprised me, given one of the designer's astounding design pedigree, but even the best have their duds sometimes.
